text:
maria: Heads up — during the INT8 bake yesterday I saw the model emit embedded NULs and weird control escapes that break our JSON postprocessing.

maria: Example from a single request (post-quant, batch size 1):
```
{"action": "create_task", "args": {"title": "Fix deploy\u0000issue", "meta": "priority:high"}}
```

maria: That \u0000 shows up sporadically and sometimes a comma turns into a stray byte so the downstream parser throws. Not consistent across seeds.

akshay: ouch. which quant config? int8 symmetric? per-channel? AWQ was disabled right?

maria: int8-gptq-ish run, per-tensor asymmetric with minmax clamping. AWQ wasn't used in this run; I was trying a faster, lower-mem path.

diane: any chance it's tokenizer alignment? control codes often surface when bpe splits a control sequence across tokens.

maria: I thought that too. I ran tokenizer roundtrip on the prompt and output; the tokenizer claims validity, but the raw token ids include 0x00 in the byte sequence after dequantization.

akshay: can you paste the raw bytes around the offending region? maybe a kernel quant rounding issue.

maria: pasted sample below (hex of post-dequant bytes):
```
... 7b 22 61 63 74 69 6f 6e 22 3a 20 22 63 72 65 61 74 65 5f 74 61 73 6b 22 2c 20 22 61 72 67 73 22 3a 20 7b 22 74 69 74 6c 65 22 3a 20 22 46 69 78 20 64 65 70 6c 6f 79 00 69 73 73 75 65 22 7d 7d
```

maria: note the 00 between 'deploy' and 'issue'.

diane: interesting — the 0x00 aligns with a token boundary where one token decodes to '\\x00issue' if you treat that byte as part of the UTF-8 stream.

akshay: could be a bad embedding table entry or a mistaken padding value creeping into KV cache. Does the runtime zero-pad any buffers and reuse them?

maria: runtime reuses buffers; we have memcpy paths that only touch used_len but not the rest. Hypothesis: dequant path doesn't zero out tail bytes after last valid token and downstream decoder reads through buffer.

diane: that matches the sporadic nature — buffer reuse across requests. If the tail bytes aren't masked, a previous request's residue could appear.

eval-bot: automated check: replayed failing sample 10x under reproducible seed -> 3/10 showed NUL insertion. Logged pmap and kernel names: matmul_q8_dequant_v2 and kv_cache_reuse true.

akshay: can you try forcing a memset of the output buffer in the runtime before decode and re-run the same sample? If it goes away, it's a reuse bug.

maria: running now...

maria: quick test: forced memset solved it for 50/50 runs locally. Will run more.

maria: longer run (200 repeats) with memset => 0/200 NULs. Without memset => 58/200.

diane: ok that strongly implicates the buffer reuse path. We need a perf tradeoff doc for zeroing vs leaving as-is.

akshay: short-term patch: add conditional zeroing when output is about to be formatted as JSON or when structured-output mode is enabled. Perf hit should be small for structured calls.

maria: agreed. I'll prepare a PR that zeroes only the decoder tail when structured-output flag is on. also add an eval test that asserts JSON validity for our structured prompt suite.

sre-bot: deploy bot: new canary build queued (rb/quant-fix-zeroing) — will run on dedicated-canary. :rocket:

diane: also add a fuzz harness that checks for ASCII control chars in final output across quant modes (INT8, GPTQ, FP8). We should cover boundary cases where token alignments change.

akshay: and capture which kernel variants are used in failures so model-onboarding sheet can flag risky kernels for structured-output workloads.

maria: filing onboarding note: "quantized-run: watch buffer-reuse artifacts; enable structured-output zeroing". I'll paste PR link when ready.

maria: tl;dr — root cause appears to be buffer reuse + dequant path not clamping tail bytes; workaround is targeted zeroing for structured outputs, long-term fix is ensure dequant path writes deterministic tail or kernel-level fix. :white_check_mark:
